office_does: A Richland City Council member is one of the city's elected, nonpartisan legislators, setting city budgets, codes and priorities; this seat carries a three-year unexpired term.
race_blurb: The seat is on the ballot because Donald Landsman, elected to it in 2025, died; interim appointee Todd Samuel finished third in the primary. Primary leader Kyle Saltz, a veteran and Hanford Patrol officer, calls for a surplus and lower taxes; PNNL scientist Mary Lipton stresses balancing growth with Richland's character.

candidates.summary: Army counterintelligence veteran, Army reservist and Hanford Patrol tactical officer who led the primary with 40%, running on lower taxes, a budget surplus, public safety and municipal-code cleanup.
highlights: Calls for a budget surplus while reducing taxes on an overburdened population [S1]
Wants to cut outdated municipal codes and bureaucracy and pledges to donate his council pay [S1]
Campaign site cites rising crime and homelessness and backs Richland police [S3]
Lost a 2025 council race (Position 6) to Kurt Maier by about 4.5 points; led the 2026 primary with 40.4% [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Explicitly calls for a surplus 'while reducing taxes on an overburdened population.'

spending.basis: Promises responsible spending, a balanced budget with surplus, and removing unnecessary bureaucracy and inefficiencies.

safety.basis: Centers law-enforcement expertise, rising crime and gang activity, support for Richland police, and safety-first handling of homelessness.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; his leadership experience is in the VFW and he lost a 2025 council bid.

candidates.summary: PNNL staff scientist, WSU adjunct professor and 30-year Richland resident who finished second in the primary, running on managing growth while preserving Richland's character, parks and riverfront.
highlights: Says Richland is 'walking a fine line between growth and maintaining its identity' and favors a balanced approach [S2]
Lists responsible growth and infrastructure, workforce development, public safety, parks and riverfront access as priorities [S1]
Emphasizes evidence-based decisions, transparency and fiscal stewardship [S1]

experience.basis: No prior public office; experience is in science, teaching and school and community volunteering.
